headline: 3 young stores to learn from
intro: Three Shopify stores launched in the last 12 months: a one-product men's fragrance brand scaled on Meta, a grill-basket brand re-pitched as a Black Friday gift, and a women's general store with no live Meta, Google or TikTok ads, where Pinterest leads social traffic.
key_takeaway: Pinterest is renaming campaign objectives: Sales and Leads replace Catalog sales and Conversions; API-built campaigns must move by 1 Feb 2027.
method: Trend Track: created after 19 Nov 2025; main market US, UK, CA or AU; traffic growth above 40% over 90 days; revenue above $40k/month; earlier stores excluded. The Pinterest pick has the Pinterest Tag, no live Meta ads and Pinterest as top social source on Similarweb (Pinterest share of paid social is an inference). Revenue, units and October traffic are estimates. *Orders estimated from units and bundles.
actions: Ask your Pinterest app or agency when they move to the new Sales objective (deadline 1 Feb 2027).
Copy BRYN's gift angle: same product, re-pitched in Q4 as “the gift he'll use for life”.
Google Shopping: set sale_price + effective date for Black Friday to earn the “Deal ends” badge.
Meta: compare Ads Manager purchases with Shopify orders; on-device measurement is on since 12 Nov.

stores.name: ASCEND SKIN

branding.label: Identity
branding.text: One product: a 140 g shea “body butter cologne” with pheromones, in scents named Zeus, Apollon and Helios, each “inspired by” a $400 designer perfume. Hero: “Pheromone body butter. Never go unnoticed again.”

branding.label: Offer
branding.text: Jar at $35 (shown against $60; the FAQ says $28). Bundles change by page: “Buy 3 get 2 free” on the homepage, “Buy 2 get 1 free” and “all 3 scents for $56” on the founder advertorial. Black Friday countdown banner.

branding.label: Trust stack
branding.text: “4.8/5 from 60,000+ ratings” next to “150,000 men made the switch”, vegan and “dermatologist-verified” badges. Guarantee varies: 30-day, 90-day and “even if opened” on different pages, while the FAQ refuses opened jars.

ads: Meta: ~3,600 live ads on 12 pages (main page 3.1M reach in 30 days), up from ~600 in September. Ads run in the US, CA, AU, NZ and most of the EU, with landing pages split across two domains (myascendskin.com and theascendskin.com).

Format: long mini-drama videos (2–5 min): a man ignored by his wife or at the gym, a stranger in Dubai reveals the “secret”, women suddenly notice him. Shorter cuts: “cologne vs. cologne” comparisons and “we made way too many jars, 75% off”.
Google Ads: 229 live ads, mostly YouTube/Display placements (“Other”), a few Search and Shopping. No TikTok account found.
lessons: A new format, not a new product: a body butter sold as a cologne that “lasts 12 hours instead of 2” gives a $35 jar a clear reason to beat a $400 spray.
Story-led video ads (several minutes long) can scale on Meta when the hook is strong: watch-time is the filter, the offer comes only at the end.

Watch out: pheromone attraction promises, unsourced skin claims (“clinically proven” on melanin-rich skin), designer-perfume names, an unverifiable Shark Tank story and contradictory guarantees are exactly what gets ad accounts and Shopify stores flagged. Learn the format, not the claims.

stores.name: BRYN
stores.origin: “Swedish brand”, US entity (House of Nordic LLC, Wyoming)

branding.label: Identity
branding.text: “Built for better, easier grilling.” Nordic story: a founder (“Anders”) who grew up grilling in Värmland, “from a garage in Värmland to the world”. Bare 304 stainless steel, wooden twist-off handle, dishwasher safe.

branding.label: Offer
branding.text: Rolling Grill Basket $37.99 (shown against $94.99), Flat Basket $39.99, Classic $37.99, Grill Spray $9.99 as the add-on. “VIP Black Friday sale, up to 60% off + free gifts”, and an “overstock flash sale” advertorial.

branding.label: Trust stack
branding.text: Lifetime guarantee (“we'll replace it, no questions, for life”), “50K+ happy grillers”, free shipping. No star ratings or press logos. The discount varies between 40% and 60% depending on the page.

ads: Meta: ~11,900 live ads on 32 pages, mostly from the page GrillMästaren (11,000 live ads, 41.5M total reach), up from ~1,900 in September. Targeting: US, AU, CA, NZ, UK in similar shares.

Top angles: “We owe you an apology… we lied” (the “lie” is that the price could not drop: 1.19M reach), the “founder overstock” 60% off, creator UGC (“a one-pot wonder, barbecue edition”), and in November a gift angle: “The gift he'll use for life”.

Google Ads: 91 live ads (Search first, then Shopping and YouTube) in the same five markets. No TikTok account found. Note: the revenue tracker's point estimate sits above its own range; treat the figure as an order of magnitude.
lessons: A small, visual problem (veggies falling through the grate) is easy to show in 3 seconds of video, and the product sells itself in the demo.
Smart seasonality: a summer product kept alive in November by re-pitching it as a gift for men, and by selling in Australia and New Zealand, where it is barbecue season.

Watch out: a “Swedish” story behind a Wyoming LLC, crossed-out prices up to $94.99, permanent “overstock” and “last time at 40% off” claims, and the “we lied” hook can trigger consumer-protection complaints. Keep the demo, drop the fake urgency.

stores.name: Thesbox

kpis.label: Active Meta ads
kpis.note: 207 short tests · no Google or TikTok ads

branding.label: Identity
branding.text: No real brand: a 534-product store aimed at women 45+ (Similarweb: 70% female, top age group 55–64), selling “easy-to-wear dresses, tops, sets” per Similarweb's summary. The homepage blocks automated reading.

branding.label: Catalogue
branding.text: Problem-solving gadgets next to clothing: heated root-lift hair clip, foot callus remover, highland-cow fabric-art kit, colour-changing foundation stick. Emoji-heavy titles, “50% OFF” banners.

branding.label: Offer
branding.text: Products at $19.99–$29.99; ad landing pages stack “up to 76% off + buy 1 get 1, buy 3 get 3”.

best_sellers.name: Birth Flower Highland Cow 3D Fabric Art Kit

ads: Pinterest: Pinterest Tag installed; Similarweb (Oct) lists Pinterest as top social network and paid social at 87.9% of desktop visits. With no live Meta, Google or TikTok ads, the paid social is most likely Pinterest Ads (inference: Similarweb does not split by network).
Meta was a test bed: 207 ads in Sep–Oct, each live 0–3 days, 747 people reached in total (women 25–65).
Trend Track and Similarweb both show a 38% drop in October after the September spike.
lessons: Pinterest's older female audience fits “fix-it” beauty gadgets and craft kits: products people save before buying.
Cheap Meta tests to pick products, then spend where the audience converts.
Caveat: no brand, stacked discounts, falling October traffic. Learn the channel fit, not the store.

pinterest_updates.title: New campaign objectives: Sales and Leads replace Catalog sales and Conversions
pinterest_updates.what: Pinterest's November developer newsletter adds SALES and LEADS as campaign objectives and marks CATALOG_SALES and WEB_CONVERSION as legacy. Every campaign built through the Ads API must be migrated by 1 Feb 2027. Reporting gains new conversion events (add payment info, add to wishlist, initiate checkout, subscribe, view content), and a Pinterest MCP for ads workflows is in invite-only testing.
pinterest_updates.why: If you launch Pinterest campaigns through a Shopify app, a feed tool or an agency, objectives and reports will change before February. Ask them now, and start adding the new events (add to wishlist, checkout) to your Pinterest Tag for better optimisation.

pinterest_updates.title: Holiday shopping tools in Pinterest's assistant, and Pinterest inventory in Google DV360
pinterest_updates.what: 12 Nov: Pinterest's shopping assistant gets trending gift guides, product comparisons and wish lists. 18 Nov: Google's Display & Video 360 buyers can now buy Pinterest premium video and display inventory with Pinterest audiences.
pinterest_updates.why: Gift guides and wish lists pull from shoppable Pins: make sure your catalogue is synced with clear titles and prices before Black Friday. The DV360 deal is for large programmatic buyers, not small stores.
pinterest_updates.source: socialmediatoday.com (12 Nov 2026) · blog.google, Google Marketing Platform November drop (18 Nov 2026)

other_updates.title: Video ads: 6 seconds can count as a ThruPlay; video audiences cut to 3 options (16 Nov)
other_updates.what: Reported on social and by PPC Land, not announced by Meta. Don't compare cost per ThruPlay across old and new campaigns. Existing 75% and 95% viewer audiences keep working for retargeting.

other_updates.title: Shopify stores enabled by default for Meta's AI shopping agent (13 Nov)
other_updates.what: Secondary source (AdsUploader, citing Sierra), not confirmed by Meta. If true, an AI agent reads your product data: check prices, stock and return policy are accurate.

other_updates.title: Holiday “Deal ends” badges are live; promotion titles can't carry dates (13 Nov)
other_updates.what: Badge needs at least 10% off, an end date within 7 days and the lowest price in 60 days. Google Ads Editor 2.14 (12 Nov) also turns on AI Max by default for new Search campaigns: check before publishing.

other_updates.title: No verified TikTok Ads product change this week
other_updates.what: The last big items (global ad network open to US advertisers, agentic AI tools) date from early October. Symphony's video upgrade from 9 Nov remains the BFCM tool to try.

sources: Trend Track (shops, sales tracker, Meta and Google ad libraries, TikTok profiles, 19 Nov 2026); similarweb.com public pages (Oct 2026); store homepages, founder and About pages (19 Nov 2026; thesbox.com blocks automated reading); community.pinterest.biz (18 Nov 2026); socialmediatoday.com (12 and 17 Nov 2026); blog.google (18 Nov 2026); jxtgroup.com weekly roundup (17 Nov 2026); adsuploader.com (15 Nov 2026); ppc.land (16 Nov 2026). Meta agent and ThruPlay items come from secondary sources.
